title: Plugins: a page is a tree of plugins
description: Templates, instant page changes and the gear page, as one plugin system. Plan; the MVP is built after a fresh review.

add.text:
**The plan in one line:** a page is a tree of plugins you can switch on and off, its own choices are saved as lines in its `page.jsonl`, and a **template is a saved plugin tree** that another page adopts in one call.

**Status:** plan, written 2026-11-09. Next comes a fresh review. If you don't answer, the MVP below gets built and demoed. Nothing is built yet.

add.title: MVP: one page shows its plugin tree, with working switches
add.description: A demo page, /live/demos/plugins/, with a Plugins panel: one row per plugin, sub-plugins nested under their parent, a switch on each. Flip one and the page changes at once, and stays changed after a reload.
add.text:
**What you would see:** the page, plus a panel beside it:

```
☑ tabs
☑ status
   ☑ voice        ← a plugin of status
☐ previews
[ Save as template… ]
```

**What a switch does:** `page.plugins.set({tabs: {enabled: false}})`. The page writes one line, so a reload keeps it, and the item tool can do the same.

**Smallest version:** three toy plugins (`border`, `badge`, `wide`) on one demo page. That proves the tree, the switch, the save and the reload without touching real pages.

**Waits on:** live-page's fold step 2, `class Page extends Pluggable(Item)` (building now). About **$5**, one Sonnet minion.

add.title: What exists: most of it is already built
add.description: core/Plugin already does plugins with switches, per page, with sub-plugins and saved choices. Page doesn't use it yet; fold step 2 connects them.
add.text:
| Piece | What it does today | Live? |
|---|---|---|
| [core/Plugin](/framework/core/Plugin/) | `Host.use(A)`, `Host.unuse(A)`, a live list of rows `Host.plugins` (`enabled`, `config`) | yes: the dev server's classes and the demo panel |
| per-page choice | `inst.plugins.set({A: {enabled: false}})` for one instance only; `inst.overrides` is plain data you can save | yes, in tests and the demo |
| **plugins of plugins** | `row.plugins` is a plugin's own list; a row is `active` only when its parent is on (`PluginEntry.js:25`) | built, unused |
| make default | `Host.make_default(inst)`: one page's choices become everyone's default | built |
| [the fold plan](/live/plan/fold/) | LivePage's extras become plugins: tabs, settings (the gear), status, pages, tasks, voice, buttons | step 2 building |
| page extensions | `core/Page/ext/` (Inbox) through `page.ext(name)` and a `{ext: …}` line; no off switch | yes; becomes plugin rows in fold step 2 |
| views in JSONL | a page line `{type: "View", content: "Hello world"}` draws a div (`Item.foreign`, [demo](/live/div-test/)) | yes |
| [core/Page/Template](/framework/core/Page/Template/) | one layout drawn many times from data rows (`clone(data)`) | yes, BigCard. **A different thing:** a repeated card, not a page template |

add.title: The shape: a page is a tree of plugins (proposal)
add.caption: Content and streaming fit the same tree: `content` is a plugin with its own plugins (previews, auto scroll), and live streaming could be a plugin a static page switches off. The content LIST itself stays a plain List: Item and List skip plugins on purpose (they're made by the thousand on replay; core/Plugin/doc/design-notes.md, "Cost").

add.title: A template is a saved plugin tree, adopted in one call (proposal)
add.caption: It is the same layering core/Plugin already has, class row → instance row, with one layer added in the middle. A template is stored as a page (its own folder and page.jsonl), so you can open it, see it and edit it like any page. A list of templates sits at /framework/core/Page/templates/.

add.title: Where you switch them: the gear page
add.description: The gear on every page opens its settings; a Plugins section there shows the tree with a switch per row, plus "Save as template" and "Make default".
add.text:
- **The gear** is the `settings` plugin from the fold plan (today LivePage's Settings + Files). Its first section is **Plugins**: the tree, a switch per row, a row opens to its config fields (`fields` on the plugin, the way the [core/Plugin demo](/framework/core/Plugin/) panel already draws them).
- **Three buttons:** *Reset* (`page.reset_plugins()`), *Make default* (`Page.make_default(page)`, every page), *Save as template* (`page.save_template(name)`).
- **Same switches for agents:** the item tool writes the same line, `item({path, set: {plugins: {tabs: {enabled: false}}}})`. You and the agent change one thing, the same way.

add.title: Views in JSONL: yes for experiments, with one limit
add.description: It already works: a line {type: "View", content: …} draws a div. Keep it to registered classes, never raw HTML, and treat it as a sketch: a good one graduates into a card type or a plugin.
add.text:
**Worth it because** an agent can sketch a layout in seconds (a div of spans, a row of boxes) without writing a page.js, and it streams like any line.

**The risks:**
- **A second HTML.** Pages made of raw divs can't be restyled or reused, and nobody can tell what they mean.
- **Unsafe text.** Raw HTML strings would be an injection path.
- **Data mixed with drawing.** A task list written as divs is no longer a task list.

**Decision:** keep `{type: "View"}` lines and allow only registered classes (View, the card types) with text content, never `innerHTML`. Nest by `content: […]`. When a sketch is used twice, it becomes a card type or a plugin; that is how an experiment gets adopted.

**Alternative:** no views in JSONL at all, cards only. Safer, but it loses the quick sketch the owner asked about.

add.title: After the review: four small merges, about $15
add.description: MVP first (the plugin tree with switches on one demo page), then templates, then the gear page, then real plugins move over. Each merge is revertible and gets a card on /live/done/.
add.text:
1. **MVP** (~$5): `page.plugins` drawn as a tree with switches on `/live/demos/plugins/`; a switch writes one line; reload keeps it. Three toy plugins. *Waits on fold step 2.*
2. **Templates** (~$4): `page.save_template(name)` writes a template page under `/framework/core/Page/templates/<name>/`; `{template: name}` on a page reads it as the middle layer. Demo: make a page from a template in one call.
3. **The gear page** (~$3): the Plugins section moves into the `settings` plugin, so every page has it.
4. **Real plugins** (~$3 each, later): tabs, status, previews move onto the tree as the fold plan lands them. The fold plan's own steps do most of this.

Instant page changes (new page, add tab, add card, full screen) need no new system: they are already one item-tool call each (card below). Only the missing ones get built, inside step 1.

add.title: The alternatives
add.description: Copy-on-apply templates, or templates as code (page.js subclasses). Both are simpler on day one; both lose the live link between a template and its pages.
add.text:
- **Copy instead of layer:** `apply("dashboard")` copies the template's lines into the page. Simpler, no lookup at load. But a template change never reaches the pages that used it, and "what came from the template" is lost. Wins if templates are only starting points.
- **Templates as code:** `class Dashboard extends Page` in a page.js. Already possible today. But an agent or the gear page can't make one, and it can't be switched per page. Wins for a template that needs real logic.
- **Every Item pluggable** (`Item extends Plugin`): tasks and cards could have plugins too, at a measured +27% cost per new Item. Start with Page and content; widen if a real need shows.

add.title: Instant page changes: all four are already one call
add.description: New page, add a tab, full screen and add a card are each one item-tool call, and open tabs redraw within about a second. The catch: under /live/, tabs and columns don't draw yet (LivePage skips them). The fold plan fixes that.
add.text:
| You want | One call (on `page`) | Works today? |
|---|---|---|
| a new page | `page.pages.add({name: "notes", title: "Notes"})` | yes, everywhere |
| add a card | `page.content.add({type: "part-card", title, text})` | yes, everywhere |
| tabs | `page.set({navigation: "tabs"})`, then each sub-page is a tab | on plain pages yes; **under /live/ no** ([demo of the gap](/live/demos/)) |
| full screen | `page.set({width: "full"})` (`narrow`, `reading`, `wide`, `full`) | on plain pages yes; under /live/ untested |

Source: [ai-api.md](/framework/core/Page/doc/ai-api.md), [words.md](/framework/core/Page/doc/words.md). **So no new system is needed.** The gap is LivePage, and fold steps 2–5 close it: once `/live/` pages are plain Pages, every word works there too. A demo page `/live/demos/instant/` showing all four, live, is part of MVP step 1.

add.title: Your October template ask was built, but it answered a different question
add.description: On 2026-10-12/13 "page templates" became `class Template extends Page`: one layout drawn many times from data (BigCard). That is a repeated card. What you're asking now, a page setup others adopt, was never planned.
add.text:
- **2026-10-12/13:** the [page-templates plan](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/12/session-87bec773/page-templates/plan.md) built `Template extends Page`, `Property` and BigCard; all five steps landed.
- **What it does:** one card layout, many data rows (`clone(data)`), with live bindings measured 5× faster than redrawing ([binding.md](/framework/core/Page/doc/binding.md)).
- **What it doesn't do:** save a page's setup (features on or off, layout, starter cards) so other pages can adopt it. No plan for that was found (searches: `template system`, `page.use(`, `save_template`, `preset`; [findings](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-page-design/page-templates/findings.md)).
- **Both keep their place:** a template (this plan) sets up a page; a Template (October) draws a repeated card inside it. **Naming risk:** two things called template. Option: call this one a *page preset* (`page.set({preset: "dashboard"})`). The plan keeps your word, *template*, for now.

tip.text:
**The plan in one line:** a page is a tree of plugins you can switch on and off, its own choices are saved as lines in its `page.jsonl`, and a **template is a saved plugin tree** that another page adopts in one call.

**Status:** plan written 2026-11-09, then checked by a fresh reviewer ([review](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-page-design/page-templates/review/review.md)). Its two fixes are in: tabs already work under /live/, and a template needs one new lookup step in core/Plugin (more on the template card). The MVP is being built now, on a demo page, without waiting for the fold plan.

mvp.text:
**What you would see:** the page, plus a panel beside it:

```
☑ border
☑ badge
   ☑ count        ← a plugin of badge
☐ wide
[ Reset ]
```

**What a switch does:** `page.plugins.set({wide: {enabled: true}})`. The page writes one line, so a reload keeps it, and the item tool can do the same.

**Smallest version:** three toy plugins (`border`, `badge`, `wide`) on one demo page. That proves the tree, the switch, the save and the reload without touching real pages.

**No wait:** the demo's page is a small host class built on core/Plugin (`class DemoPage extends Plugin`), so it starts now. When the fold plan makes `Page` pluggable (step 2, building), the same three plugins attach to a real Page unchanged. About **$5**, one Sonnet minion.

template.caption: **This part is new code, not reuse** (the review caught it). core/Plugin looks a value up in two steps today: the page's own choice, else the class default (`PluginEntry.get_one`, core/Plugin/PluginEntry.js:13). A template needs a third step in the middle, kept apart from the page's own choices, so a page can tell "the template said so" from "I chose this". About 20 lines in PluginEntry and Plugin, agreed with live-page first. A template is stored as a page (its own folder and page.jsonl), so you can open, see and edit it like any page. The list sits at /framework/core/Page/templates/.

steps.text:
1. **MVP** (~$5, starting now): a plugin tree with switches on `/live/demos/plugins/`, on a small demo host built on core/Plugin; a switch writes one line; a reload keeps it. Three toy plugins. Plus `/live/demos/instant/`.
2. **Templates** (~$5): one new lookup step in core/Plugin (own choice → template → class default), agreed with live-page; `page.save_template(name)` writes a template page under `/framework/core/Page/templates/<name>/`; `{template: name}` on a page adopts it. Demo: make a page from a template in one call.
3. **The gear page** (~$3): the Plugins section moves into the `settings` plugin, so every page has it. *After fold step 2.*
4. **Real plugins** (~$3 each, later): tabs, status, previews move onto the tree as the fold plan lands them. The fold plan's own steps do most of this.

Instant page changes (new page, add tab, add card, full screen) need no new system: they are already one item-tool call each (card below).

instant.description: New page and add a card are one item-tool call each; a tab is two; full width is one. Under /live/, all of them work except full width, and columns, a left rail and placed files don't draw yet either. The fold plan fixes those. [Live demo](/live/demos/instant/).

| tabs | plain page: `page.set({navigation: "tabs"})`. Under /live/: `page.pages.add({name})`, then `page.tab({name, tab: true})` | yes, everywhere ([demo](/live/demos/instant/)) |

Source: [ai-api.md](/framework/core/Page/doc/ai-api.md), [words.md](/framework/core/Page/doc/words.md). **So no new system is needed.** Fold steps 2–5 close the rest: once /live/ pages are plain Pages, every word works there.
